tagline: Two old highways, one buffalo trace, west to the Wabash.
intro: The byway is a Y of two old highways. US 50 sets out from Lawrenceburg on the Ohio, and US 150 from New Albany and Clarksville across the river from Louisville. They meet at Shoals and run on together to Vincennes on the Wabash. US 150 keeps roughly to the line of the Buffalo Trace, a route first trodden by bison and later used by pioneers and stagecoaches.
Between Shoals and Loogootee the road runs beside the East Fork of the White River. Shoals once made mother-of-pearl buttons out of the river's mussels.

moments.title: Paoli
moments.text: A Quaker town laid out in 1816, known for the Pioneer Mothers Memorial Forest, a surviving fragment of the virgin oak forest that once covered southern Indiana.

moments.title: Shoals
moments.text: Outside town Jug Rock, a 42-foot sandstone column, stands free of its cliff under a flat cap long known as the stopper, and the high school teams are the Jug Rox.

moments.title: Vincennes
moments.text: French fur traders founded it in 1732 where the Buffalo Trace crosses the Wabash, and it stayed the capital of Indiana Territory until 1813.
